name: SPACE
ability_definition: The ability to imagine how something will look after it is moved around or when its parts are moved or rearranged.

task_realism.reasoning: The MRT, MPFB and PTT subtests adapt validated human psychometric tests of visualization, so they target the right cognitive operations: rotating objects, fitting pieces together, and taking another viewpoint. However, they use abstract block figures and geometric shapes. Workplace visualization involves real objects, such as assembling parts, reading blueprints, packing loads, planning furniture layouts, CAD edits, and surgical approaches. That domain gap is substantial.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Testing uses isolated, static rendered images with no task context, tools, feedback loops, or consequences. In real work, visualization is done alongside physical manipulation, sketching, 3D software, and iterative checking. The benchmark also offers text-only versions that simplify the tasks further, and the headline average mixes in non-visualization tasks, which weakens how well the measured conditions match real work.

construct_coverage.reasoning: The small-scale battery covers the core facets of the O*NET definition: mental rotation (moving objects), form board (rearranging parts), and perspective taking (seeing objects from another viewpoint). It covers less of multi-step assembly, dynamic motion, and domain-specific transformations. The aggregate score is also diluted by large-scale navigation and attention/working-memory tasks, so only the subscores cleanly measure visualization.

format_match.reasoning: Inputs are rendered test figures and outputs are forced-choice answer selections. These are standardized-test artifacts, not real work artifacts such as drawings, models, assembly instructions, or physical arrangements. Nothing in the tasks requires producing or manipulating a transformed representation.

transferability_reasoning: SPACE is the most construct-aligned benchmark for Visualization because it directly adapts classic human mental rotation, form board, and perspective-taking tests. Transfer to real work is limited by abstract stimuli, multiple-choice formats, context-free testing conditions, and an aggregate score that mixes in non-visualization tasks. It is a reasonable probe of core mental-transformation ability but a weak proxy for applied workplace visualization.

2024.metric: average accuracy (%) across the 10 small-scale SPACE tasks, multimodal presentation; chance is below 25%
2024.human_reference: General adult workforce. Classic psychometric visualization tests (MRT, form board, perspective taking) are normed on general adults and students.
